# KRAKEN v1.1 against SESTINA v1.0: an independent check of the cross-engine claim

*FishLab, 2 September 2026. Generated by `research/kraken-check/make_report.py` from the artifacts in `research/kraken-check/`; no number below was typed by hand.*

## Verdict

The paper's headline cross-engine claim — KRAKEN beats SESTINA v1.0 by **+2.3466** [+2.2928, +2.4004] sets per game, 63.0% of decided sets, 80.4% of games won — **does not survive an independent measurement, and the reason is identified.**

1. **In FishLab's arbiter**, with KRAKEN played exactly as its own integration guide requires, KRAKEN loses: **-0.648** [-0.740, -0.556] sets per game and **40.3%** [38.3%, 42.3%] of games over 5,400 games under FishLab's rules, and -0.759 [-0.842, -0.676] sets per game over 6,000 games under KRAKEN's own declare-on-turn dialect.
2. **In KV's own arbiter** (their Python engine, their rules, their bridge revision 2, fresh seeds) the paper's number reproduces: **+2.446** [+2.327, +2.565] over 2,000 games, with SESTINA declaring correctly only 78.0% of the time.
3. **The difference is a defect in their bridge into SESTINA**, `fish4/dylan_v07.py`: it resets SESTINA with its *current* hand as if that were the hand it was dealt, then replays the whole public history on top. Correcting that one line — passing the hand as dealt, which is what FishLab's own driver passes — and re-playing the identical deals in their arbiter moves the result by **-3.149** [-3.307, -2.991] sets per game (paired, 2,000 games). Under the corrected bridge KRAKEN loses in their arbiter too: **-0.703** [-0.828, -0.578] sets per game, 39.5% of games; on 8,000 further fresh games, -0.570 [-0.632, -0.508].
4. The two arbiters then agree. SESTINA's declaration accuracy in their arbiter rises from 78.0% to 96.9%, which is what it measures at natively (98.0% in FishLab); the '78.9%' the paper builds its mechanism story on is the bridge, not the engine.

The forced-endgame bridge repair the paper describes (their revision 2) is real but immaterial at this scale: giving the mover FishLab's full willingness ladder moves the margin by -0.003 [-0.008, +0.002].

Read against the paper: it claims KRAKEN takes 63.0% of sets and 80.4% of games; the package README's dialect table claims +2.375 sets per game under exactly FishLab's rules ("both sides may declare off-turn, your dialect, played fairly") and +2.675 when nobody declares off-turn. Neither dialect comes within thirty standard errors of either figure. The mirror cell is the control that the harness itself is symmetric; the lineage cells place KRAKEN on this repository's ladder for context.

For reference, the paper's own 10,000-game journal (`results/mega_match_journal.jsonl` upstream, copied under `research/kraken-check/upstream/`) gives +2.3466, 63.0% of sets, 80.4% of games, SESTINA declaring right 78.9% and hitting 48.1% of asks; the `rev2` row is that measurement on fresh seeds, and it agrees.

The forced-endgame variant is a null. The dealt-hand variant flips the sign of the result, removes almost all of SESTINA's ownership-class errors (declaring a half-suit an opponent still holds a card of), restores its ask hit rate, and brings its declaration accuracy to where FishLab measures it natively. SESTINA's *voluntary* declarations under rev 2 are wrong more than a fifth of the time — so the paper's mechanism story ("knowing when a half-suit is finished", the 18-point gap, the 57% of the margin that is 'declaration accounting') describes a policy whose posterior had been corrupted before it was asked anything.

## 4. The same defect at the level of single decisions

`agree_probe.cpp` plays native SESTINA in FishLab's arbiter under KV's rules (declare on turn only) against KRAKEN, and at every one of its 6,403 on-turn decisions (120 games) also serialises the position exactly as `dylan_v07.py` does and asks KV's own shim binary twice: once with the current hand (their rev 2) and once with the hand as dealt. Hypothetical declarations are scored against the true hands.

| | native SESTINA | shim, current hand (rev 2) | shim, dealt hand |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| declarations over these decisions | 580 | 793 | 673 |
| of which wrong | 8 (1.4%) | 176 (22.2%) | 38 (5.6%) |
| agrees with native on declare / don't declare | — | 6127 of 6403 (95.7%) | 6310 of 6403 (98.5%) |
| declares when native does not | — | 239 (158 wrong, 134 of them naming a half-suit an opponent holds) | 93 (30 wrong, 22 ownership) |
| declines when native declares | — | 26 | 0 |
| both declare, different allocation | — | 11 | 0 |
| same ask as native | — | 4141 of 5733 (72.2%) | 4815 of 5733 (84.0%) |
| first decision of a game identical (same random state) | — | 359 of 360 | 359 of 360 |

The first-decision row shows the rest of their serialisation is faithful: with the random stream in the same state the shim answers what the native agent answers. The residual ask disagreement under the dealt hand is the restarted random stream (a fresh agent per decision), which the `dealtseed` row above prices in play.

## 5. The mechanism, in their code and ours

`fish4/dylan_v07.py::_feed` writes `HAND <bitmask>` from `obs.hand`, and `Observation.from_state` sets `hand=state.hands[player]` — the hand *now*. `external_v07/shim_decide.cpp` then calls `agent->reset(seat, hand, rules, seed)` and replays every event. In this engine `Agent::reset` receives the hand as dealt (`game.hpp`, `Game::setup`), and `Knowledge::init` (`belief.hpp`) marks every card not in it as *unknown, and never mine*.

The damage is done in `Knowledge::onEvent` (`belief.hpp:189-201`). Every ask by seat *p* in half-suit *S* yields a legality certificate — *p* held some other card of *S* at that moment — built over the cards of *S* whose owner is still unknown and whose candidate mask includes *p*. If SESTINA later took card *c* of *S* from *p*, the bridge has already marked *c* as SESTINA's since the deal, so *c* is excluded from the certificate; the certificate is now over the wrong cards, and when exactly one candidate remains the code pins it to *p* as a deduction (`setOwner`, line 200) — a card *p* never held. Symmetrically, a card SESTINA was dealt and lost is treated as never its own. The exact counting and the Sinkhorn fit that SESTINA's declaration gate reads then reconcile a constraint set no deal satisfies, and the errors that come out are ownership-class: declaring half-suits an opponent still holds a card of.

The paper measured this signature without recognising it (§11.9, "What their errors are made of"): every one of the 398 cards inside SESTINA's ownership errors was one that had *never publicly moved*, and the errors concentrate in half-suits where KRAKEN had asked and SESTINA had later taken a card off KRAKEN — a rate ratio of 67. That is precisely the population of certificates the bridge corrupts: KRAKEN's ask created the certificate, SESTINA's later capture of a card of that half-suit is what the current-hand reset mis-files, and the phantom deduction lands on a card that never moved. The paper's hypothesis that SESTINA's inference treats "at least one" as "exactly one" is not what the code does.

Everything downstream of this in the paper inherits it: the head-to-head, the declaration decomposition (57% of the margin as 'declaration accounting'), the acquisition table, the dialect-gap table in the README, the contestation-term port (Table 18, measured against a corrupted SESTINA), and the exhibition on their website, which reconstructs every session from the public log through the same `_feed`.

## 6. What this does and does not establish

- **Refuted:** that KRAKEN beats SESTINA v1.0 by about 2.35 sets per game, takes 63% of sets, wins 80% of games, or has an 18-point declaration-accuracy edge over it. In both arbiters, once the bridge passes SESTINA the hand it was dealt, KRAKEN loses roughly 0.65–0.75 sets per game and about 60% of games.
- **Not tested here:** KRAKEN's internal lineage claim (+2.412 sets per pair against its own v0.3 champion), its exact-inference, posterior-quality and endgame-solver results. None of them involve SESTINA, and nothing here bears on them.
- **Not claimed:** a global ranking. One foreign opponent is one opponent; SESTINA's own report declines the same claim for the same reason.
- **Fairness to KRAKEN in FishLab:** it is polled off-turn as required, its cards are named, its errors abort the run, it receives the true holders on a wrong declaration as in its own engine, it has no clock, the mirror cell reads as it should, and its declaration accuracy is *higher* here than in its own arbiter. If KV's project finds a defect in `kv6.hpp` the way this check found one in theirs, the paired instrument to price it is the same.

## 7. The repair, and how to reproduce

`research/kraken-check/dylan_v07_dealt_hand.patch` is a minimal patch to upstream `fish4/dylan_v07.py` (bridge revision 3): recover the dealt hand by undoing the seat's public transfers newest-first, and pass that. Their `tests4/test_dylan_bridge.py` will want a case for it. The rows in §3 were produced with the same logic as a subclass (`research/kraken-check/kvarena/e2_variants.py`), with a forward-replay check that the dealt hand reproduces the current hand on every decision (zero mismatches).

```bash
# FishLab arbiter (from engine/): one 600-game block under KRAKEN's dialect
./fish match --a=kraken --b="$(python3 -c 'import json;print(json.load(open("fishbot_v07.json"))["spec"])')" --games=100 --rotations=6 --threads=14 --seed=778001 --no-out-of-turn --json
python3 research/kraken-check/run_e1.py 14                       # the whole battery of section 2
# KV's arbiter: their package + their shim (built against engine/src) in a gitignored work dir, then their design
sh research/kraken-check/stage_kvarena.sh && cd engine/external/kvarena-work
PY=../kv-venv/bin/python                           # the vendored interpreter with numpy
E2_VARIANT=rev2      $PY run_e2.py 1000 6 910000 ../../../research/kraken-check/e2_rev2.jsonl        # their bridge as published
E2_VARIANT=dealthand $PY run_e2.py 1000 6 910000 ../../../research/kraken-check/e2_dealthand.jsonl   # one line repaired, identical deals
python3 research/kraken-check/analyse.py && python3 research/kraken-check/make_report.py docs/KRAKEN-CLAIM-CHECK.md
```
